newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak central bank says Ekoagrobanka move pre-emptive.
newsitem.headline: Slovak central bank says Ekoagrobanka move pre-emptive.

text.p: The National Bank of Slovakia (NBS) on Monday said it revoked the banking licence of the Slovak branch of troubled Czech Ekoagrobanka to pre-empt "negative influences" from entering the Slovak banking sector.

"The entire situation did not guarantee that some negative influences would not touch the whole Slovak banking sector through the bank's organisation structures," a senior NBS official, who asked not to be named, told Reuters.

The NBS withdrew the branch's licence on Sunday because it failed to show positive results in the recovery process after being placed under forced administration in January this year, following a similar move by the Czech central bank over the parent bank.

The NBS move has been questioned by some Czech banking officials since Ekoagrobanka's Czech licence has not been revoked, and the bank has shown initial signs of a recovery after one of its competitors, Union Banka, took a stake in it.

"So far we don't have information on the Czech central bank's (CNB) attitude or intentions in the case at the moment, but we didn't want to wait until the negative influences would affect the entire banking sector," the NBS official said.

"Further development now depends on Ekoagrobanka's reaction, and it is, to some extent, still open. We are waiting for its project, which may be, for example, bank's liquidation or entry of some other bank operating in Slovakia," he added.

Union Banka had said it intended to maintain its entire network of branches in both the Czech Republic and Slovakia, but the official said the NBS had not been sold on the ideas put forward to strengthen the bank.
"We found the Union Banka ideas as not effective enough to guarantee the successful recovery process in the bank," the NBS official said.
He said deposits of Ekoagrobanka's clients should not be affected by the central bank's move, but declined to elaborate.
